symptom: A `split type $V` with no branch for $V's own entity (CE0090), a branch on an entity that is not that entity or a specialization of it (CE0774: an unrelated entity, the subject's generalization, a sibling) or the same entity twice (CE0771) passed `check` and `exec`; `mx check` rejected the microflow.
file: mdl/executor/validate_inheritance_splits.go ValidateInheritanceSplits (MDL109), wired in validate_program.go with the lazy project opener. Tests validate_inheritance_splits_test.go; fixtures mdl-examples/bug-tests/split-type-invalid-branches.fail.mdl and split-type-branches.mdl
cause: Only the spelling of the split was checked (MDL065). The builder emits the (empty) flow unconditionally, so CE0089 — the code this started from — cannot be produced by MDL, and nothing judged which entities the branches name.
insight: **The code in the coverage list was unreachable; its siblings were not, and the old records described an older build.** CE0089 is the missing (empty) flow, which the builder always adds. The 11.13.0 records said every subtype needs a branch; re-measured on 11.16.1, a missing subtype (direct or deeper) builds clean and only the subject's own entity is required, so reporting missing subtypes would have been a false error on every partial split, and the help text, an AST comment and the MDL065 message were corrected. The subject's entity is taken from the flow's parameters and its retrieve-first or create results only; the branch entity's chain from the script, then the project, and an incomplete chain is never read as unrelated.
